questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the given sentence.

The war was followed by a long period of __prosperity.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Failure**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"prosperity"** means a state of being successful, usually by making a lot of money. (समृद्धि )

 
 
• **Example: **The country enjoyed a period of peace and prosperity after the war.
 
 
 
• **"Failure" **refers to the lack of success or the inability to meet an expectation. (असफलता)
 
 
• **Example: **The project ended in failure due to poor planning.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'prosperity' **is **'failure'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Failure**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Security **(सुरक्षा): The state of being free from danger or threat.

 
 
• **Example:** The government has increased security at all airports.
 
 
 
• **Secure **(सुरक्षित): Fixed or fastened so as not to give way, become loose, or be lost.
 
 
• **Example: **Please make sure the doors are secure before you leave.
 
 
 
• **Affluence** (धनाढ्यता): The state of having a great deal of money; wealth.
 
 
• **Example:** His affluence is evident from the luxurious lifestyle he leads.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Martha made pancakes yesterday.

options.text: Pancakes had been made by Martha yesterday.
Pancakes were being made by Martha yesterday.
Pancakes were made by Martha yesterday.
Pancakes was made by Martha yesterday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Martha made pancakes yesterday."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "pancakes" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "made" to "were made" (past simple passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Martha."
 
• Ensure the time phrase "yesterday" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Pancakes were made by Martha yesterday."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Pancakes had been made by Martha yesterday." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).
 
• **Option 2: **"Pancakes were being made by Martha yesterday." – Incorrect tense (past continuous passive).
 
• **Option 4: **"Pancakes was made by Martha yesterday." – Subject-verb agreement error.

questions.question:
In the given question, a statement divided into different segments is given. Rearrange all the segments to form a coherent

statement.

O: also benefit from knowing

P: there are several reasons

Q: why even parents would

R: more about how and why

S: children do the things that they do
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence construction begins by stating the existence of multiple reasons, establishing the context:

 
 
• "There are several reasons why even parents would also benefit from knowing more about how and why children do the things that they do."
 
 
 
• **Sentence P is the first sentence** as it introduces the existence of several reasons:
 
 
• "There are several reasons"
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q follows** as it begins to explain who benefits from these reasons:
 
 
• "why even parents would"
 
 
 
• **Sentence O is the next part** as it expands on the benefits that parents would have:
 
 
• "also benefit from knowing"
 
 
 
• **Sentence R follows** as it begins to detail what parents would know more about:
 
 
• "more about how and why"
 
 
 
• **Sentence S is the concluding part** as it completes the thought with the specific actions of children:
 
 
• "children do the things that they do"
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **PQORS**.

 

**Coherent sentence after rearrangement**:

"There are several reasons why even parents would also benefit from knowing more about how and why children do the things that they do."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Radhika stood by Monica's side __through thick and thin.__

options.text: Under easy situations wherein she could ensure Monica's safety and security
In all the happy moments, personally spending most of her time
Under all conditions, no matter how challenging or difficult
In the moments when Monica couldn't complete some simple tasks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"through thick and thin"** means supporting someone in all circumstances, good or bad, no matter how difficult. (अच्छे और बुरे समय में)

 
 
• **Example: **True friends will stand by you through thick and thin, no matter what happens.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Under easy situations wherein she could ensure Monica's safety and security** (सिर्फ आसान परिस्थितियों में समर्थन देना): Supporting only in simple and safe conditions.

 
 
• **Example:** She helps her friends only when things are going smoothly.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: In all the happy moments, personally spending most of her time** (सिर्फ खुशहाल क्षणों में साथ रहना): Being with someone only during joyful times.
 
 
• **Example:** She enjoys celebrating with friends in their happy times.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: In the moments when Monica couldn't complete some simple tasks** (सिर्फ तब मदद करना जब वे सरल कार्यों में असफल हों): Helping someone only when they struggle with simple tasks.
 
 
• **Example:** She only steps in to help when her friend faces minor difficulties.

questions.question:
Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. Identify the part that has an error. Select 'No error' if there is no error.

Although the team had __trained diligently for months__, they __had still overwhelmed__ by the opponent's unexpected tactics.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The error lies in the phrase **“had still overwhelmed”**.
 
• The verb form **“overwhelmed”** is incorrect here as it does not match the intended passive voice structure.
 
• The correct form should be **“had still been overwhelmed”**, indicating that the team was affected by the opponent’s tactics.
 
• In the past perfect tense, when expressing a passive action, the structure should be: **had + been + past participle**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“Although the team had trained diligently for months, they had still been overwhelmed by the opponent's unexpected tactics.”*

questions.question:

In November, Lakshman fell (P) / with fever (Q) / seriously ill (R) and pneumonia (S).
questions.solution:

__
 
• The sentence begins with "In November, Lakshman fell," which is correctly indicated by **part (P).**** **
 
• Following the subject, "seriously ill" **(R)** continues the logical sequence, making it clear how Lakshman fell.
 
• **The next part,** "with fever" **(Q)** adds more detail about Lakshman's condition.
 
• **Ending with **"and pneumonia" **(S)** completes the sentence by specifying the illnesses.

Therefore, the correct answer is **P, R, Q, S.**

• **Option 4 (R, Q, S, P):** This option starts with "seriously ill with fever and pneumonia In November, Lakshman fell," which does not make sense contextually.
